descriptions: Define a dynamic mass density measurement at the active pit using a vibrating tube Coriolis flowmeter, with moving average transformation and Gaussian uncertainty.

Define a dynamic mass density measurement at the active pit hydraulic element using a vibrating tube Coriolis flowmeter principle, classified as a derived continuous data type with mass density as the authoritative quantity. Apply a moving average transformation, assign Gaussian uncertainty with a mean value, and transmit the data via top-side telemetry. Associate the measurement with the inlet hydraulic branch, link it to corresponding temperature and pressure measurements as references, and specify Baroid as the instrumentation provider.

descriptions: Define a dynamic flow curve measurement at the active pit using concentric cylinder technology, supplied by Baroid and transmitted via topside telemetry.

Define a dynamic flow curve measurement at the active pit logical element, associated with the inlet hydraulic branch and the top-of-string junction, utilizing the concentric cylinders measurement principle. Specify the data as a direct measurement with JSON data type, apply a moving average transformation, and link it to derived temperature and pressure measurements at the active pit, both of which are also smoothed with moving averages. The instrumentation is provided by Baroid, and the flow curve data is transmitted via topside telemetry.

descriptions: Define a dynamic plastic viscosity signal for the active pit, computed via a Bingham plastic model and transmitted via topside telemetry.

Define a dynamic drilling signal representing plastic viscosity at the active pit logical element, using the concentric cylinders measurement principle and referenced to local temperature and pressure measurements. The data should be computed by a Bingham plastic model fitter, processed with a moving average transformation, characterized by Gaussian uncertainty, associated with the inlet hydraulic branch at the top of string junction, and provided by Baroid via topside telemetry.

descriptions: Define a dynamic fluid shear stress signal at the active pit using a Bingham plastic model with moving average smoothing and Gaussian uncertainty.

Configure a dynamic drilling signal for fluid shear stress at the active pit, computed by a Bingham plastic model fitter using the concentric cylinders measurement principle and referenced by local temperature and pressure measurements. Apply a moving average transformation and Gaussian uncertainty to the signal, associate it with the inlet hydraulic branch, transmit it via top side telemetry, and identify Baroid as the instrumentation provider.

descriptions: Define a dynamic drilling signal for fluid shear stress measured at the active pit using the concentric cylinders principle, with yield power law rheology and top-side telemetry transmission.

Create a dynamic drilling signal representing fluid shear stress, measured at the active pit logical element using the concentric cylinders measurement principle and associated with the inlet hydraulic branch. The data must be computed using a yield power law rheological model, smoothed with a moving average transformation, and assigned Gaussian uncertainty. It must reference local temperature and pressure measurements for correction, be transmitted via top-side telemetry, and be provided by Baroid as the instrumentation company.

descriptions: Define a computed fluid shear stress data point at the active pit based on yield power law behavior using concentric cylinders measurement.

Create a continuous computed data point for fluid shear stress at the active pit logical element, associated with the inlet hydraulic branch, using a yield power law rheological model and concentric cylinders measurement principle. The consistency index is computed by a model fitter within a Baroid-supplied measurement device, referenced against measured temperature and pressure at the pit, processed with a moving average, assigned Gaussian uncertainty, and transmitted via topside telemetry.

descriptions: Configure a dynamic drilling signal for the yield power law flow behavior index measured at the active pit using a concentric cylinders principle.

Define a dynamic drilling signal for the yield power law flow behavior index as a dimensionless quantity measured at the active pit using a concentric cylinders principle, computed by a model fitter subsystem, and transmitted via top-side telemetry. Apply a moving average transformation and associate Gaussian uncertainty to the signal, while linking it to derived temperature and pressure measurements at the active pit, the inlet hydraulic branch, and the Baroid instrumentation provider.

descriptions: Define a dynamic drilling signal for fluid shear stress computed using a non-Newtonian rheological model and controlled by rotational speed.

Define a dynamic drilling signal representing fluid shear stress as a continuous computed data type. Apply a concentric cylinders measurement principle where the rotational speed serves as a controlling set point, establishing a dependency for the signal. Calculate the value using a non-Newtonian fluid rheological hypothesis and associate Gaussian uncertainty with the computed data, assigning the computed value as the uncertainty mean.

descriptions: Define a dynamic mass density measurement at the active pit using a vibrating tube Coriolis flowmeter, associated with the inlet hydraulic branch and transmitted via top side telemetry.

Create a dynamic drilling signal for mass density at the active pit, measured by a device using the vibrating tube Coriolis flowmeter principle and located at the active pit logical element. Associate this density measurement, along with concurrent temperature and pressure measurements from the same device, with the inlet hydraulic branch, applying a moving average transformation and Gaussian uncertainty to the density signal. Link the temperature and pressure measurements as references for the density signal, assign the density measurement to the Baroid instrumentation provider, and transmit the density data via top side telemetry.

descriptions: Define a dynamic flow curve signal for the active pit using concentric cylinders measurement, provided by Baroid and transmitted via top-side telemetry.

Create a direct measurement flow curve for the active pit that uses the concentric cylinders measurement principle and is provided by Baroid. The signal should be associated with the inlet hydraulic branch upstream of the top-of-string junction, transmitted by top-side telemetry, and processed with a moving average transformation. It must reference continuous temperature and pressure measurements taken by the same hydraulic device located at the active pit logical element.

descriptions: Configure a dynamic drilling signal for plastic viscosity at the active pit, computed via a Bingham plastic model and transmitted via top-side telemetry.

Define a dynamic drilling signal for plastic viscosity located at the active pit, where the value is computed by a Bingham plastic model fitter using the concentric cylinders measurement principle. The signal is associated with the inlet hydraulic branch upstream of the top of string junction, references local temperature and pressure measurements, applies a moving average transformation, and is assigned Gaussian uncertainty with the viscosity data point as the mean. Top-side telemetry transmits the data, and Baroid is identified as the providing instrumentation company.

descriptions: Define a dynamic drilling signal for the fluid shear stress yield point at the active pit, computed using a Bingham plastic model and transmitted via topside telemetry.

Create a dynamic drilling signal for fluid shear stress representing the yield point of the drilling fluid at the active pit, which is computed by a Bingham plastic model fitter using a concentric cylinders measurement principle. The signal is defined as a continuous data type with Gaussian uncertainty, a moving average transformation, and a temperature reference, located at the active pit and associated with the inlet hydraulic branch, and provided by Baroid.

descriptions: Define a fluid shear stress measurement at the active pit using a yield power law model, with associated temperature and pressure references.

Define a continuous fluid shear stress data point at the active pit logical element, computed using a concentric cylinders measurement principle and a yield power law rheological model where the shear stress serves as the yield stress parameter. Apply a moving average transformation and assign Gaussian uncertainty to the data, which is transmitted via top side telemetry and associated with the inlet hydraulic branch. Link this shear stress signal to measured temperature and pressure references at the active pit, with all data provided by the Baroid instrumentation company.

descriptions: Define a dynamic consistency index signal for fluid shear stress at the active pit, computed via a yield power law model and transmitted by topside telemetry.

Establish a dynamic drilling signal representing the yield power law consistency index of fluid shear stress, located at the active pit logical element and associated with the inlet hydraulic branch at the top of string. The signal is computed using a yield power law model fitter with the concentric cylinders measurement principle, provided by Baroid, and transmitted via topside telemetry. It includes a moving average transformation and Gaussian uncertainty centered on the measured value, with temperature and pressure reference measurements also taken at the active pit and associated with the inlet branch.

descriptions: Define a dynamic drilling signal for the yield power law flow behavior index at the active pit, computed from pressure and temperature measurements using a concentric cylinders principle.

Create a dynamic drilling signal representing the yield power law flow behavior index, which is a dimensionless quantity computed by a model fitter at the active pit logical element. The calculation uses the concentric cylinders measurement principle and references local temperature and pressure measurements, all associated with the inlet hydraulic branch. The signal is smoothed with a moving average, includes Gaussian uncertainty, is transmitted via top-side telemetry, and is provided by Baroid.

descriptions: Define dynamic drilling signals for base star measured raw weight and its moving minimum derivative, located at the bottom hole assembly and transmitted via mud pulse telemetry.

Establish continuous derived measurement instances for base star measured raw weight and base star measured minimum raw weight, both identified as weight on bit drilling quantities and mechanically located at the bottom hole assembly. Apply a moving minimum transformation to the raw weight measurement to derive the minimum weight signal, assign Gaussian uncertainty to the minimum weight measurement with the measurement itself as the uncertainty mean, and specify mud pulse telemetry as the transmission method for the minimum weight signal, with Halliburton designated as the instrumentation company providing both measurements.

descriptions: Define a computed continuous data point for accumulated cuttings recovery volume at the shale shaker, processed by an image interpreter and transmitted via topside telemetry.

Create a computed continuous data point representing the accumulated volume of cuttings recovered, classified as a drilling quantity and located at the shale shaker element where drilling fluid is present. The data point should be linked to a dynamic drilling signal, transmitted by topside telemetry, and associated with Gaussian uncertainty. Apply a moving average transformation to the signal, identify the fluid component as cuttings, and designate an image interpreter as the computation unit supplied by the instrumentation company.

Configure a dynamic drilling signal representing the theoretical accumulated cuttings recovery volume as a continuous data point located at the shale shaker element. Ensure the signal is transmitted via top-side telemetry and provided by the instrumentation company.

descriptions: Configure a downhole equivalent circulating density signal derived from pressure measurements at the bottom hole assembly annulus, incorporating top liquid level corrections.

Define a dynamic drilling signal for downhole equivalent circulating density with mass density as the measurable quantity and apply a moving average transformation. Establish a continuous downhole pressure measurement at the bottom hole assembly annulus under circulating conditions with drilling liquid and air present, also applying a moving average. Use the downhole pressure, top liquid level true vertical depth (referenced to a vertical depth frame), and top liquid level reference pressure (absolute reference) as inputs for a pressure to equivalent density transformation, ensuring the downhole equivalent circulating density depends on these inputs and is provided by the D-WIS internal service.

descriptions: Define an angle magnetic flux density quantity with radian tesla as its SI unit.

Define angle magnetic flux density with dimensions of mass, inverse time squared, inverse electric current, and angle; use radian tesla as the SI unit and associate radian gauss, radian Maxwell per square centimetre, radian milligauss, radian millitesla, radian microtesla, radian nanotesla, and radian weber per square metre as alternatives. Also associate degree tesla, degree weber per square metre, degree gauss, degree Maxwell per square centimetre, degree milligauss, degree millitesla, degree microtesla, and degree nanotesla, using zero-offset scaling with the declared conversion factors for both radian-based and degree-based units.

Associate it with all listed degree- and radian-based units formed from second, minute, hour, and day intervals, and configure each conversion with zero offset and its specified multiplicative scale factor.

descriptions: Define energy density with dimensions of mass per length per time squared and use joules per cubic metre as its International System of Units unit.

Configure energy density as mass per length per time squared, with joules per cubic metre as the International System of Units unit, and associate it with joule, kilojoule, megajoule, gigajoule, calorie, kilocalorie, and British thermal unit scales across cubic metres, litres, cubic feet, cubic inches, and separate United Kingdom and United States gallons. Apply zero offsets and the specified scale factors to all energy-density units, and assign symbols such as J/m³, kJ/L, BTU/ft³, and Cal/gal(US).

Specify energy density dimensions as mass per length-time squared
Establish joule per cubic metre as the SI unit
Associate energy density with joule, kilojoule, megajoule, and gigajoule units
Associate energy density with calorie, kilocalorie, and British thermal unit units
Associate energy density units with cubic metre, litre, cubic foot, cubic inch, and gallon volumes
Specify separate United Kingdom and United States gallon energy-density units
Configure zero offsets and scale factors for all listed energy-density units
Assign symbols including J/m³, kJ/L, BTU/ft³, and Cal/gal(US) to units

descriptions: Define a mass density gradient per length quantity with kilograms per cubic metre per metre as its International System of Units unit.

Define a mass density gradient per length quantity with mass exponent one and length exponent negative four, using kilograms per cubic metre per metre as the International System of Units unit. Associate specific gravity per metre and specified metre intervals, metric density gradients over metre intervals, United Kingdom and United States pounds-per-gallon gradients over specified foot intervals, and pound-per-cubic-foot, pound-per-cubic-inch, and pound-per-cubic-yard gradients over the declared foot intervals, with zero-offset linear conversion factors for every alternative unit.

descriptions: Configure frequency as a measurable engineering quantity with hertz as its SI unit.

Configure frequency with a time exponent of negative one and associate it with hertz, reciprocal second, kilo-, mega-, giga-, and terahertz units, as well as rotation, revolution, stroke, shock, and angular-rate units expressed per second, minute, hour, or day. Apply linear conversions with zero additive offsets and the configured multiplicative factors for every frequency unit.

Associate frequency with rotation, revolution, stroke, and rate-per-hour units

Associate frequency with radian and degree angular-rate units
Configure linear conversion factors for all frequency units

descriptions: Define pressure with its physical dimensions, pascal as the International System of Units reference, and the supported engineering unit conversions.

Define pressure with mass, length, and time dimensions of one, negative one, and negative two, respectively, and establish the pascal as its reference unit. descriptions: Define time as a base quantity with seconds as its international-system unit and support the configured time units.

Define time with a dimension exponent of one and establish seconds as its international-system unit. Associate seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, shakes, nanoseconds, picoseconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, fortnights, common, sidereal and synodic months, common quarters, common, Gregorian-average, Julian, leap and tropical years, decades, centuries, millennia and million years with time; configure zero-offset linear conversion factors for each unit and assign the corresponding display symbols.
intent_sketch: Define time as the configured base quantity
Specify the time dimension exponent as one
Establish seconds as the SI unit for time
Associate seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, shakes, nanoseconds, and picoseconds with time

Assign configured display symbols to the corresponding time units

Associate decanewton metre (daN•m), kilogram-force metre (kgf•m), kilonewton metre (kN•m), foot-pound (ft•lbf), kilofoot-pound (kft•lbf), newton decimetre (N•dm), newton centimetre (N•cm), newton millimetre (N•mm), and inch-pound (in•lbf) with torque using conversion factors of 0.1, 0.10197162129779283, 0.001, 0.7375621492772655, 0.0007375621492772656, 10, 100, 1000, and 8.850745791327185, respectively.

descriptions: Define volumetric flow rate as a physical quantity with cubic metres per second as its SI unit.

Define volumetric flow rate with dimensions of three for length and negative one for time, establish cubic metres per second as the SI unit, and associate it with the supported second-, minute-, hour-, day-, and year-based volume-flow units, including metric, cubic-foot, UK gallon, US gallon, barrel, and scaled daily units. Configure zero-offset linear conversions for all associated units.

descriptions: Define wave number with reciprocal metre as its SI unit and support reciprocal-length units for engineering use.

Define wave number as a physical quantity with reciprocal metre as its SI unit, and associate it with reciprocal metric units from reciprocal decimetre through reciprocal picometre, reciprocal astronomical units such as reciprocal astronomical unit, reciprocal light-year, and reciprocal parsec, and reciprocal imperial, nautical, Scandinavian, and specialized imperial length units. Configure linear conversions from each unit to reciprocal metres using zero additive offsets and length-based multiplicative factors, with appropriate reciprocal-length symbols for measurement representation.
intent_sketch: Define wave number as the configured physical quantity
Establish reciprocal metre as the SI unit for wave number
Associate wave number with reciprocal metric units from decimetre through picometre
Associate wave number with reciprocal astronomical units including astronomical unit, light-year, and parsec
Associate wave number with reciprocal imperial, nautical, and Scandinavian length units
Associate wave number with reciprocal specialized imperial units including inch per thirty-second, mil, thou, hand, and furlong
Configure linear conversions from each reciprocal length unit to reciprocal metres
Set zero additive offsets and length-based multiplicative factors for all reciprocal units
Specify reciprocal-length unit symbols for representing wave number measurements

descriptions: Define a derived black stream electronic temperature measurement with moving average processing, Gaussian uncertainty, and wired pipe telemetry transmission.

Create a derived measurement for the black stream electronic temperature, specifying it as a temperature drilling quantity with JSON data type. Apply a moving average transformation and assign Gaussian uncertainty defined by a continuous standard deviation data point. Link the measurement to wired pipe telemetry for transmission, associate it with the string hydraulic branch downstream of the top of string and the annulus hydraulic branch upstream of the annulus outlet, locate it mechanically at a pipe section, and assign the instrumentation provider as the NOV company.

descriptions: Define a continuous dynamic drilling signal for the overall maximum caving size at the shale shaker, computed by an image interpreter and associated with Gaussian uncertainty.

Create a continuous data point for the overall maximum caving size, classified as a small length quantity and linked to the corresponding dynamic drilling signal. The data point represents cuttings, a component of the drilling fluid located at the shale shaker logical element, where it serves as a hydraulic estimation. It is transmitted via topside telemetry, processed with a moving maximum transformation, and characterized by Gaussian uncertainty where the mean is the caving size itself and the standard deviation is a separate continuous length signal. The data is computed by an image interpreter and provided by an instrumentation company.

descriptions: Define a dynamic signal for the overall average cutting size at the shale shaker, computed by an image interpreter and transmitted via topside telemetry.

Configure a continuous dynamic drilling signal representing the overall average cutting size as a small length quantity, which is a hydraulic estimation located at the shale shaker element and concerns cuttings as a component of the drilling fluid. The signal is computed by an image interpreter, provided by an instrumentation company, and transmitted via topside telemetry. Additionally, apply a moving average transformation to the signal and assign a Gaussian uncertainty profile where the mean matches the overall average cutting size and the standard deviation corresponds to the sigma cutting size signal.

descriptions: Define a derived pressure measurement at the active pit with Gaussian uncertainty, moving average transformation, and top-side telemetry transmission.

Create a derived pressure measurement located hydraulically at the active pit and associated with the inlet hydraulic branch upstream of the top of string junction. The measurement is taken by a device classified as a hydraulic logical element, provided by the intelligent mud system, and transmitted via top-side telemetry. Include a moving average transformation for the pressure data and define Gaussian uncertainty using the measured pressure as the mean and a separate standard deviation data point.

descriptions: Define a continuous radial acceleration measurement at the swivel sub, transmitted via top side telemetry, with Gaussian uncertainty.

Specify a continuous radial acceleration measurement for the drilling process, associated with a radial reference frame and located mechanically at the swivel sub within the rotating drive system. The measurement is transmitted via top side telemetry, provided by an instrumentation company, and characterized by Gaussian uncertainty where the mean matches the measured value and the standard deviation is defined by a separate data point.

descriptions: Define a stick-slip indicator computed from rotational speed at the bit hole assembly, transmitted via mud pulse telemetry with Gaussian uncertainty.

Configure a computed stick-slip indicator as a dimensionless dynamic drilling signal at the bit hole assembly, derived from a rotational speed measurement classified as an angular velocity drilling quantity. The indicator serves as the output of a computation estimator that uses the rotational speed as input, is transmitted via mud pulse telemetry, linked to a stick-slip drilling incident, and characterized by Gaussian uncertainty where the indicator is the mean and its standard deviation is a separate dimensionless data point, with Halliburton designated as the instrumentation provider for all associated data points.

descriptions: Define a dynamic drilling signal for measured peak radial acceleration at a pipe section, classified as a continuous data type with Gaussian uncertainty, transmitted via mud pulse telemetry and provided by Halliburton.

Define a dynamic drilling signal for measured peak radial acceleration, classified as a continuous data type associated with the acceleration quantity, located at a pipe section mechanical element within a radial reference frame, and provided by Halliburton. Apply a moving maximum transformation to the measured radial acceleration to derive the peak value, configure the transmission of this peak acceleration via mud pulse telemetry, and specify a Gaussian uncertainty model for the measurement where the standard deviation is associated with the uncertainty model.

descriptions: Define the bottom hole assembly minimum raw torque measurement with its associated uncertainty, telemetry, and provider details.

Establish a dynamic drilling signal for the bottom hole assembly minimum raw torque as a derived measurement of torque drilling quantity, which is the output of a moving minimum transformation applied to the raw torque signal. Define the raw torque as a dynamic drilling signal of torque drilling quantity serving as the input to the transformation, and specify a drilling data point for the standard deviation of the minimum raw torque as torque drilling quantity. Model the uncertainty of the minimum raw torque as a Gaussian distribution using the minimum raw torque as the mean and the standard deviation data point as the standard deviation, transmit the minimum raw torque via mud pulse telemetry, locate all three data points at the bottom hole assembly, and associate Halliburton as the instrumentation provider for each.
